McLaren.summary: McLaren’s aero package has been tweaked across the car – the rear‑wing endplates have been reshaped, the floor and its under‑tray have been fresh‑molded, and both front‑ and rear‑corner barge‑boards have been revised – to tighten up airflow and give the car a more stable rear‑end and sharper front bite. At the same time, the team has opened up the brake‑cooling ducts to keep the brakes from overheating on the high‑speed, heavy‑braking circuit. Together, these changes should boost corner‑entry grip and keep the power unit running cooler, giving McLaren a better shot at defending or climbing the podium this weekend.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has bolted a small extra winglet onto the centre of the rear wing to dial‑in the right amount of drag for this track, widened the rear exit on the engine cover to keep the car cooler, and blended the little tail winglet into the rear‑wing brace for a stiffer rear end. Together these changes should make the car more stable on corner exit and keep the power unit at its sweet spot, giving the team a little extra grip and straight‑line speed for the weekend’s races.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked the rear wing – reshaping the little pylons and the flap itself – and also refined the floor’s diffuser shape. These changes tighten the car’s aerodynamic grip, giving the RB more stable downforce especially through fast corners. In short, the RB should be easier to drive and able to extract a few extra tenths on the current circuit.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has given the rear wing a fresh makeover – the flaps now have extra little bits at the back and the end‑plate shape has been reshaped, plus new support pillars and an optional “winglet” that can be tucked into the side‑pod area. These tweaks should give the car a more stable rear end, especially in high‑speed corners, helping drivers keep the car glued to the track and extract more grip when it counts this weekend.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has swapped in a fresh rear‑wing layout and a re‑shaped floor winglet, both aimed at reducing drag on this circuit. The slimmer rear‑wing flap and the new floor geometry should give the car a little more straight‑line speed without sacrificing downforce, helping the team extract extra pace in the long straights and improve overall balance for the weekend’s race.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Red Bull has added small winglets to the roll‑hoop, shaping the air that reaches the car’s rear and giving a subtle boost in overall grip. The rear wing’s end‑plate shape and auxiliary bits have been tweaked to fine‑tune the down‑force balance for the track’s specific corners, while extra cooling louvers let the power unit stay in the optimal temperature window. Together these changes should make the RB a bit more stable through high‑speed sections and keep the engine humming efficiently for the weekend’s demands.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has given the car a full‑aero makeover – a slimmer, longer nose and re‑shaped front wing/endplates push more clean air over the front, while the floor, diffuser and rear wing get fresh vanes, winglets and a reshuffled chord to boost down‑force and rear‑end stability. The side‑pod inlet, rear‑suspension geometry and tiny tweaks to the rear‑corner and beam wing tighten the car’s balance, meaning better grip through high‑speed corners and less tyre‑wear on the sprint‑type circuit. In short, the updates should translate into quicker lap times and a more predictable handling package for this weekend’s race.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has tweaked the rear wing by reshaping the SM fairing and adding a small gurney‑flap. The changes give the car a bit more rear‑end grip and stability, especially through the fast corners at this circuit. In practice, that translates into better tyre wear and more confidence when battling for position this weekend.

Audi F1 Team.summary: Audi’s F1 car now sports a tweaked rear‑wing endplate, a subtle shape change that smooths the airflow over the rear wing. The adjustment reduces drag while keeping down‑force intact, so the car will be quicker on the straights without losing grip in the corners. In short, Audi expects a faster lap time and better tyre preservation for this weekend’s race.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac has reshaped the front‑corner brake‑cooling ducts – tweaking the inlet scoop and the exit holes – so the brakes stay cooler under heavy braking. This lets the drivers dig deeper into the corners without fearing brake fade, giving them a confidence boost when pushing late. In short, the car should be able to attack the brakes a bit harder this weekend.
